CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  (Notice No. N2M25-87)

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a special meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held
on Monday, July 7, 2025, commencing at 2:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California pursuant to the order of the
Mayor of the City of Alhambra, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal Code, and
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

An agenda of such special meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

Dated:  July 2, 2025
Notice No.  N2M25-87

  MISSION STATEMENT

  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and
  quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive
  business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our
  community.

Watch and listen to the meeting as follows:
Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://cityofalhambra-org.zoom.us/j/89725039693?pwd=2AZqEhDOMceGq5FmEjYLbJ4woMXwZb.1
Webinar ID: 897 2503 9693, Passcode: 281050
Or by telephone by dialing (833) 548-0276 (Toll Free) or (833) 548-0282 (Toll Free) or (877) 853-5257
(Toll Free) or (888) 475-4499 (Toll Free) or +1(719) 359-4580 or +1(309) 205-3325 or +1(253) 215-8782
or +1(346) 248-7799 or +1(646) 931-3860 or +1(301) 715-8592 or +1(312) 626-6799 or +1(646) 558-
8656 and entering Webinar ID: 897 2503 9693 and Passcode: 281050. Please Note: All members of
the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can proceed. If there are
technical difficulties with Zoom during the meeting, the meeting will proceed regardless. Meetings can
also be viewed via livestream here: https://www.spectrumstream.com/streaming/alhambra/live.cfm
Addressing the Council:
In person: Section 2.04.210 of the Alhambra Municipal Code establishes the procedures for addressing
the Council. Any person wishing to address the Council during the meeting should complete a Speaker
Request Card and submit it to the City Clerk so the City Council knows you wish to speak. When called
upon by the presiding officer, please step to the podium.
Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the “Raise
Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will unmute speakers
participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your time to speak.
Remarks are limited to 5 minutes; however, the presiding officer may either extend or reduce the
maximum time to such period of time as the Council may determine.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Council who refuses to stop speaking after his/her
time has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede the
progress of the City Council meeting who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such
behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers upon direction of the presiding officer.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or his/her designee, shall be Sergeant-at-Arms of the
Council meetings. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding
officer for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the Council meeting.

Persons Authorized to be Within Rail: No person, except City official or their designees, shall be
permitted within the rail in front of the Council Chamber without the express consent of the Council.

Agenda Tracking Numbers: All numbers listed in bold after the title of each Agenda item are City Clerk
tracking numbers that are used for filing and research purposes.

   AGENDA
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  July 7, 2025
  2:00 p.m.

  ROLL CALL:  Maza, Maloney, Wang, Andrade-Stadler, Lee

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-87

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City
Council being held this afternoon pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

PRESENTATION

1.  DISCUSSION REGARDING FEDERAL IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT ACTIVITIES
  – F2M25-7

  At the June 23, 2025 City Council meeting it was requested staff bring back information
  on recent Federal immigration enforcement activities within the City. Staff will provide
  information regarding Federal immigration enforcement in the City; the Alhambra Police
  Department’s operations in accordance with the California Values Act (SB54); the City
  Council’s previous public affirmations of the City’s adherence to the California Values
  Act (SB54); notable bills pending in the California legislature, SB805 (Pérez) and SB627
  (Weiner); and, helpful resources staff has identified for those impacted by recent events
  including, but not limited to, Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles, Immigrant Defenders
  Law Center, National Immigration Law Center, Coalition for Human Immigrant Rights
  (CHIRLA) and Central American Resource Center of Los Angeles (CARECEN). After
  Council discussion, it is requested the Council provide direction to staff on an updated
  statement, pending legislation, a resource webpage, or other action deemed
  appropriate.

  Recommended Action:  City Council to provide direction to staff, such as issuing
  an updated statement, support pending legislation, create a resource page on the City’s
  website, or other activities deemed appropriate.

CLOSED SESSION & CITY ATTORNEY ANNOUNCEMENT re SAME - F2M25-14

The City Council will move into a closed session pursuant to applicable law, including the Brown
Act (Government Code Sec. 54950, et seq.) for the purposes of conferring with the City’s Real
Property negotiator, and/or conferring with the City Attorney on potential and/or existing
litigation, and/or discussing matters covered under Government Code Section 54957
(Personnel), and/or conferring with the City’s Labor Negotiators as follows; provided, however,

  3
7-7-25
 prior to moving into closed session, the City Attorney shall make any announcements required
by the Brown Act pertaining to such closed session matters:

  Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to Govt. Code Section 54956.9(d)(4): 1 matter.

RECONVENE & CITY ATTORNEY REPORT: In the event the City Council moves into a
closed session, the City Council and the City Attorney shall report upon the closed session if
required.

ADJOURNMENT

  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the City Council meeting
agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at www.cityofalhambra.org and you
will be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the subscription service. Pursuant to
Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items for regular meetings of the
Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to that meeting, will be made
available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.

Broadcast of Meeting: A live video stream of each Council meeting is available through the City’s
website. The regular meetings of the Alhambra City Council are recorded and are broadcast on
Charter Channels 3 and 182 at 7:30 p.m. on Thursdays and Mondays following the meeting.
Recordings are also available for viewing by the public on the City of Alhambra’s website, at the
Alhambra Public Library and, upon appointment, in the City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City
meeting (including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-
5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

Translation Services Requests: If you require translation services in order to participate in a
meeting please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 570-5090. All requests for translation services
shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting. If translation is not
requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the City Council meeting, staff will try to accommodate the
request if possible.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

  MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  July 7, 2025
  2:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:06 p.m., on Monday, May 12, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Principal Planner McCurley, Director of
Public Works and Utilities Ahlen, Chief of Police Kennedy, Battalion Chief Brown, Director of Library
Services LohGuan, Director of Human Resources Ko, Manager Analyst Alvarez

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-87

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this afternoon pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

PRESENTATION

1.  DISCUSSION REGARDING FEDERAL IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT ACTIVITIES –
  F2M25-7

  City Manager BINNQUIST delivered a staff report. At the June 23, 2025 City Council meeting
  it was requested staff bring back information on recent Federal immigration enforcement
  activities within the City. Staff, including City Attorney MONTES and Chief of Police
  KENNEDY, provided information regarding Federal immigration enforcement in the City; the
  Alhambra Police Department’s operations in accordance with the California Values Act
  (SB54); the City Council’s previous public affirmations of the City’s adherence to the California
  Values Act (SB54); notable bills pending in the California legislature, SB805 (Pérez) and
  SB627 (Weiner); and, helpful resources staff has identified for those impacted by recent events
  including, but not limited to, Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles, Immigrant Defenders Law
  Center, National Immigration Law Center, Coalition for Human Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA)
  and Central American Resource Center of Los Angeles (CARECEN). After Council discussion,
  it was requested the Council provide direction to staff on an updated statement, pending
  legislation, a resource webpage, or other action deemed appropriate.

  Public Comment:

  The following people expressed concern about the safety of the community, spoke
  against recent federal immigration enforcement actions and spoke in favor of the
  community resolution submitted to Council:

  1) Elsa Guttierez-Aviles, 3401 Julep Place
  2) Arlene Rios, 101 S. Cordova St.

  1
7-7-25
   3) Nora Hernandez, 1128 N. Monterey St.
  4) David Bond also requested further restrictions against masked vigilantes and bounty
  hunters acting on behalf of ICE.
  5) Bill Kelly, 1852 Oxley St., South Pasadena
  6) Beverly Murata, 13 Palmetto Dr., also requested the Police Department verify the identity
  of federal agents.
  7) Michael Alexander Jones, 200 N. 5th St., also requested the Police Department verify the
  identity of federal agents.
  8) Ivonne
  9) Prranit
  10) Pablo Garcia, 1017 S. 1st St.
  11) Edward Escarcega also criticized the recent statement released by the city for not
  speaking out against immigration enforcement actions.
  12) Emily Greenfield, resident of Pasadena, also requested the Police Department verify the
  identity of federal agents
  13) Angela, resident of Monterey Park, also spoke regarding statements made by the city of
  Monterey Park and requested the Police Department verify the identity of federal agents
  14) Mimi Li, 619 S. Chapel Ave.
  15) Melissa Michelson, representing SGV Progressive Alliance
  16) Marco S., representing the Peace and Freedom Party, also criticized the recent statement
  released by the city for not speaking out against recent actions, criticized the Police
  Department for their inaction and criticized the police and prison system.
  17) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St., also spoke regarding a new path to citizenship,
  the need for DACA students to receive citizenship, the need for a reaffirmation of the 14th
  Amendment protecting birthright citizenship, and continued to speak regarding the history
  of immigration in the United States.
  18) Natalie Zarowni, 701 Westminster Ave., also requested better communication between
  the City and the community regarding this topic.
  19) Kristin Keenan, 233 S. Meridian Ave., also spoke regarding the need for law enforcement
  to defend the Constitution, enforcement of California law SB 830.10 which requires law
  enforcement to show identification, and requested the Police Department verify the identity
  of federal agents.
  20) James Johnson, via Zoom, also requested the Police Department verify the identity of
  federal agents.
  21) Ari Gutierrez Arambula, via Zoom, also requested greater communication between the
  Police Department and the community and spoke regarding the economic impact of fear
  within the community.
  22) Raul Barrera, via Zoom, also criticized the statement released by the City.
  23) Jasmin, a resident of Alhambra, also spoke regarding the need to protect constitutional
  rights and requested the Police Department verify the identity of federal agents.

  Public comment received via email and on file in the City Clerk’s office:

  1) Melissa Michelson, submitted a draft resolution titled, “City of Alhambra Condemns
  Aggressive and Non-Transparent Federal Immigration Enforcement Tactics, Reaffirms
  Commitment to Constitutional and Community Safety Principles, and Directs Proactive
  Local Response Measures,” on behalf of the SGV Progressive Alliance, Alhambra Tenants
  Union, Alhambra Community Group, and the Northeast Los Angeles Alliance for
  Democracy. A copy of the draft resolution is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  2) Gerry Fagoaga wrote in support of the community resolution.

  Discussion: Council each addressed the concerns of the community and the fears
  surrounding separation of families, racial profiling, individuals impersonating federal agents,
  and broad sweeping immigration enforcement actions. Council each expressed their own

  2
7-7-25
   concerns with recent events. Council also each shared their personal stories. Councilmember
  MAZA and Mayor LEE shared their immigration stories. Vice Mayor MALONEY shared his
  mother’s story as a Japanese American family incarcerated during World War II. Council also
  thanked the Police Department for their work and emphasized their role in keeping the
  community safe.

  Mr. MAZA and Chief KENNEDY discussed potential traffic citations for tinted windows on cars,
  per California law. They also discussed the request for Police officers to verify the identity of
  federal agents. Chief KENNEDY clarified that under federal law, federal agents are not
  required to produce their identification. Councilmember WANG and Chief KENNEDY
  discussed APD’s current protocol in responding to calls of people impersonating an officer or
  unmarked suspicious cars. Ms. WANG and Chief KENNEDY discussed reports on social
  media regarding ICE raids and Chief KENNEDY confirmed that Alhambra Police Department
  was not aware of any broad sweeping immigration enforcement in Alhambra. He stated that
  APD checked into some of the social media posts, that there had been targeted operations,
  and that when APD contacted federal agencies for confirmation they sometimes provided
  information. Chief KENNEDY confirmed that APD had not received any calls for kidnapping.
  Ms. WANG and City Attorney MONTES discussed California penal code and federal
  regulations regarding border patrol and federal immigration officers. Ms. WANG addressed
  the public and emphasized the importance of calling the Police department to report suspicious
  activity, regardless of immigration status. She stated that Alhambra could not solve national
  problems, but that the City could ensure local practices reflect the local values of safety,
  dignity, and due process for everybody who resides in Alhambra.

  Mr. MALONEY discussed the limitations faced by APD in interfering with federal agencies and
  the ways in which the City could better serve the community. He spoke regarding the statement
  released by the City and the resolution presented by community groups. Mr. MALONEY
  suggested the City could combine the concepts and statements from both in a responsible
  way. He requested a more robust list of City resources, specifically resources for the AAPI
  population, and requested that all information be provided in multiple languages.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER referred to the statement released by the National
  League of Cities and listed instances of immigration enforcement which she had either
  witnessed personally, was verbally informed of, or had seen on social media. She echoed her
  colleagues and spoke regarding the responsibility of the City and specifically the Police
  Department, the responsibility of federal law, and the need for federal agents to identify
  themselves. She requested that Council consider adopting the resolution presented by the
  community groups with possible addendums, require that all law enforcement officers wear a
  badge, make 911 the official number for the public to call for assistance with suspicious activity,
  and that staff to look for funding to help support ongoing needs of the immigrant community in
  collaboration with the Alhambra Unified School District and All Soul’s Church. She referred to
  the recent “Know Your Rights” workshop held at the Alhambra Civic Center Library and
  discussed other library resources. She went on to suggest that the Library provide citizenship
  classes, that the City provide online support, and that Council support SB 805 and SB 627.
  She requested that Council support the community resolution.

  Mayor LEE spoke regarding the challenges of recognizing misinformation which could cause
  more fear. She thanked Ms. Andrade-Stalder for her information and shared her concerns
  regarding families separated by immigration status or those who have been detained. She
  stressed that should the public hear about ICE activity, they should verify the situation. Ms.
  LEE and Chief KENNEDY discussed Homeland Security’s process in providing information to
  the City, the calls received by APD, and Police response. Ms. LEE agreed with her colleague’s
  comments and requested that the statement released by the City be updated to include
  information for the public. When asked regarding the community resolution by Mr. MAZA, Ms.

  3
7-7-25
   LEE stated that she could not approve adopting the resolution because she did not agree with
  the entirety of the document.

  After some discussion, Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to approve the resolution but
  added that it should be further reviewed by the City Attorney to verify the legality. Mr.
  MALONEY made reference to specific sections of the resolution and made several
  suggestions to clarify statements after legal review and combine or omit statement which were
  redundant. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. MONTES discussed the exploration of legal remedies. Mr.
  MALONEY suggested resolved clause #6 be changed to “Explore legal avenues to address
  impacts on cities and their residents.” Mr. MALONEY and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  discussed monitoring and recording incidents. Mr. MALONEY suggested all language
  specifically identify federal immigration enforcement in the City. Mr. MALONEY, Chief
  KENNEDY, and Mr. MONTES discussed Police Department policy in verifying warrants. Mr.
  MALONEY suggested changing the language in resolved #3 to “The Police Department will
  request a copy of warrant from any purported immigration officer and verify that it has been
  signed by a judge. Ms. BINNQUIST and Mr. MALONEY discussed this suggestion with regards
  to other calls made to the Police Department.

  Ms. WANG stated that she supported the spirit and intent of the draft resolution but that she
  wanted to steer clear of legal ramifications. She suggested staff further review the document,
  write a new resolution which would combine the statement released which was supported by
  Council, and return with the new draft resolution at the next regular City Council meeting for
  review. Ms. LEE, Ms. WANG, and Mr. MAZA discussed Ms. Wang’s suggestion, the current
  motion on the floor made by Ms. Andrade-Stadler. Mr. MAZA and Ms. LEE supported Ms.
  Wang’s suggestion. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER withdrew her motion, agreed with Ms. Wang’s
  suggestion, and further suggested that staff carefully review resolved statement #3 regarding
  the monitoring and verification. Mr. MALONEY also supported Ms. Wang’s suggestion. Council
  continued to discuss Ms. Wang’s suggestion and directed staff to return with a modified
  resolution based on their comments.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed staff to return with a modified resolution based on
  Council comments.

  Vote: Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CLOSED SESSION & CITY ATTORNEY ANNOUNCEMENT re SAME - F2M25-14

City Attorney MONTES identified those items listed on this evening’s agenda which would be
discussed in Closed Session as follows:

  Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to Govt. Code Section 54956.9(d)(4): 1 matter

whereupon at 5:09 p.m. the City Council moved into closed session pursuant to applicable law,
including the Brown Act (Government Code Sec. 54950, et seq.) for the purpose of conferring with the
City Attorney.

7-7-25
 RECONVENE & CITY ATTORNEY REPORT: At 5:31 p.m. the City Council moved out of closed
session with Councilmembers Lee, Andrade-Stadler, and Maza present. Councilmembers Wang and
Maloney were absent.

ADJOURNMENT: At 5:31 p.m. there being no further business for the Council to transact, the Mayor,
with the consent of the City Council, adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
